messages.subject: Forcing rhdel() & EC2 DFS increase
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am running a large data set that is about 12TB.  The machines that I have have a capacity of about 4TB of HDFS space.
All of the data set that make up 12TB is not required by me for the entire run. I only need about 624GB for ever run and I have about 33 runs. So i was wondering if there is a way to force rhdel() ? Force hadoop to reclaim the space immediately or at least before I am in a real bad state with regard to space?

The second question that I had was about EC2 space allocation. Rightscale version of Ubuntu allocated only about half the available diskspace on EC2. is there a way to increase this allocated space? Or should I not be concerned about it as hadoop will grow as and when the data pour in? The hadoop used on right scale is cloudera version 3 release 5.

Any inputs would be really helpful.

Thank you
Ashrith

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Hbase table connection issue using rbase.
messages.subject_clean: [rhipe] Hbase table connection issue using rbase.
messages.body_plain:
This worked at  point in time. Never tried it again.

#####################################
## Create  a table
####################################
library(rJava)
library(rbase)
hb <- rb.init()
crash.models <- rb.table.new <http://rb.table.new>(hb,"crash.models",model, meta, additional)

###############################################################################
## Inserts Data Into Hbase
## Run Once For a Reduce (many reduce keys)
## If workload is too much, crashe ..
## Now aggregate into data frames, build a model, and insert into HBase
###############################################################################
rsetup <- expression(reduce={
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(mgcv))
  library(rJava)
  library(rbase)
  hb <- rb.init()                                     ## Initialize connection to Hbase
  crashmodels <- rb.table.connect(hb,"crash.models")  ## Connect to table
  rhsz <- function (x) .Call("rh_sz",x); rhuz <- function(x) .Call("rh_uz",x)
})
m <- rhmap({
  rhcollect(k$sig, data.frame(off=k$off,hod=k$hod, dow=k$dow,count = r,stringsAsFactors=FALSE))
})
x <- rhoptions()$templates$raggregate({
  rhcounter("explosive","allsigs",1)
  adata <- do.call(rbind, unlist(adata,rec=FALSE))
  if(nrow(adata) >= (minpoints)){
    rhcounter("explosive","validsigs",1)
    adata <- adata[order(adata$off),]
    rownames(adata) <- NULL
    adata$weights <- sapply(1:nrow(adata),function(r) if(r <= (nrow(adata) - minpoints)) 0.5 else 1)
    model0 <- runExpression(suppressMessages(gam(count  ~ off + s(dow,bs='cp',k=7)+ s(hod, bs='cp',k=24)
                  ,family=poisson(link=log)
                  ,scale=-1,gamma=1.4
                  ,weights=weights
                  ,data=adata,method='ML')))
   crashmodels$putOne(key=reduce.key, values=list("model:gam"=serialize(model0,NULL) ,"model:data"=adata))
  }
},combine=FALSE)
res <- rhwatch(map=m, reduce=x,setup=rsetup,input=z, param=list(runExpression=runExpression,minpoints=25),read=FALSE)

################################################################################
## Example code to retrieve the models (in the R console, if using
## $get in a RHIPE job, there is no need for un=rhuz,sz=rhsz in the
## crashmodel$get call)
################################################################################

library(rJava)
library(rbase)
hb <- rb.init()
crashmodels <- rb.table.connect(hb,"crash.models")
f<-crashmodels$get(list("QTMLGrabMutex","_wcsicmp"),what="model:gam")
j <- lapply(f, function(r) unserialize(rhuz(r$"model:gam")))

####################################################
## Make a backup, so it doesn't get overwritten
###################################################
setup <- expression(map={
    library(rJava)
    library(rbase)
    hb <- rb.init()
    crashmodels <- rb.table.connect(hb,"crash.models.backup")
    rhsz <- function (x) .Call("rh_sz",x); rhuz <- function(x) .Call("rh_uz",x)
  })
m <- rhmap({
  d1 <- lapply(r, rhuz); names(d1) <- names(r)
  crashmodels$putOne(rhuz(k), values=d1)
})
mapred <- hbasemap(table    = "crash.models" ,colspec = c('model:'))
z <- rhwatch(rhmr(map = m,reduce=0,setup=setup
                    ,inout    = c(NA,'seq')
                    ,jarfiles = "/user/sguha/share/rhipecrashreport
